answer.verdict: Kept all four fixes. Fight seconds 50-94 mean fps: baseline 20.33, GIF zero-copy 22.42, UNPACK fast path 22.91, MFIFO span reuse 22.93, timer batch 21.78. Timer IRQ returns/bits stayed 0 and timer_late stayed 0 (103952464 flushes). Menu and fight shots stayed the same blank PrintWindow on every run.

drainMfifo clears member m_mfifoPacket (capacity kept) and appends ring spans, then one processVIF1Data. fromSPR copies contiguous scratch/ring spans and markModified once per span. mfifoContigQwords returns 1 unless rbor&rbsr==0.
DIRECT/DIRECTHL truncation forwards the available qwords and breaks. It does not call carryFrom. A split processVIF1Data would drop the rest.

MFIFO run logs/grok/game-thread-fixes-3, exe 48433152 at 02:34:14, same GS backend mtime 02:23:29 and ps2_audio.cpp 01:49:51. Seconds 50-94 mean 22.93, 88-94 mean 18.43, 100-119 mean 19.00, sec40=59, sec95=19, last 119=20. Profile 6295: memcpy 14.2%, processVIF1Data 2.0%, advanceEeTimers 2.6%, memmove 0.6%, NtWait 25.6%.
MFIFO last mem snap drains=2165520 bytes=7783769248 spr_calls=2165520 spr_qwords=32937834. IRQ 0.

advanceEeTimers adds eeCycles to m_eeTimerDebt and applies ticks only when debt >= m_eeTimerLimit. flushEeTimerDebt runs before timer register read and write. A nonzero flush mask is latched for the next advanceEeTimers. FQC is cleared only when m_gifFqcPending was set by processPendingTransfers.

Timer run logs/grok/game-thread-fixes-4, exe 48453120 at 02:43:02. gs_cpu_backend.cpp had changed to 114459 bytes at 02:38:14. Seconds 50-94 mean 21.78 (n=45, min 15, max 32), 88-94 mean 18.14, 100-119 mean 18.10, sec40=53, sec95=18, last 119=18.

Timer profile 6510 samples: NtWait 27.6%, memcpy 13.9%, GSMem::writeImageTransfer<19> 5.2%, IopKernel::beginNextReady 3.4%, processVIF1Data 1.8%, memmove 0.8%. advanceEeTimers is below the 0.5% cutoff (MFIFO profile had it at 2.6%).
Timer snaps: timer_irq_returns=0, timer_irq_bits=0, timer_late=0 on every snap including the last. Last timer_flush=103952464.
Shots 40/95/145 of runs 1-4 are 6185-byte white windows titled PS2-Recomp | SCES_50878. Run 0 shots are 6134-byte white windows of the same title. Run 4 shot_40 was viewed and is that blank window.

fix.change: If drainImmediately and m_queue is empty, call m_processFn on the caller pointer and return. Non-empty queue still copies so drain() can sort PATH3 IMAGE ahead of PATH2 DIRECTHL.
UNPACK vl==0, mask off, mode 0/3, cl>=wl: V4 cl==wl memcpy with one VU wrap; V4 otherwise per-vector 16 bytes; S-32 broadcast; V2/V3 memcpy 8 or 12 bytes so unread lanes stay. Slow loop unchanged.

fromSPR MFIFO copies contiguous scratch and ring spans and markModified once per span. drainMfifo appends those spans into m_mfifoPacket (clear keeps capacity) and still makes one processVIF1Data or one PATH3 submit.

EE timer checkpoints accumulate until cyclesUntilNextEeTimerInterrupt, then one applyEeTimerTicks. Timer read/write flushes first. A flush IRQ is latched and returned on the next advanceEeTimers. GIF_STAT FQC is cleared only on the next advance after processPendingTransfers writes it. TEKKEN4_GT_STATS adds timer_late and timer_flush.

contra: DIRECT truncation does not use m_vif1Carry (ps2_vif1_interpreter.cpp:648-667), so drainMfifo stays one buffer. Per-span processVIF1Data would drop a command that straddles the 8-byte TTE insert and the following qwords.

GIF seconds 88-94 mean 17.00 versus baseline 21.57 at the same key times, while seconds 50-70 were faster (peak 34 vs 22). The later window is a further-progressed round. 8379124/8388608 submits were immediate, so the copy path was not what the fight was doing.
fight_profile3 seconds 90-91 were 15 and 18 fps. This baseline's seconds 88-94 were 21-23. Different binary.

Runs 0-4 never showed a menu or a fight in the shot. All are a white client area in a PS2-Recomp window (6134 bytes on run 0, 6185 bytes on runs 1-4). logs/camera_ours1/shot_95s.png was a real Kazuya vs Law frame on another build. The display path is not in the owned files. Unchanged here means the capture stayed blank.

gs_cpu_backend.cpp changed between exes: 114958 bytes at 02:02 (baseline and GIF), 116773 at 02:23 (UNPACK and MFIFO), 114459 at 02:38 (timer). UNPACK's processVIF1Data drop 6.0% to 2.2% is in owned code. Its fps move and the timer fps move are mixed with that GS edit.

Timer IRQ evidence is 0 versus 0. No snap in runs 0, 1, or 4 had a nonzero timer_irq_returns, timer_irq_bits, or timer_late. The counter cannot show a positive rate. 103952464 flushes means timer registers are hit often, so many updates still happen on the read or write rather than inside advanceEeTimers.

Run 0 had no profile because shot 108 closed the process at perf second 95, before the 88:12 window plus SymFromAddr. Runs 1-4 added shot 145 and did print a profile. fight_profile3's memcpy 5.9% / RtlAllocateHeap 3.3% / processVIF1 7.1% is a different binary without TEKKEN4_GT_STATS.

Timer seconds 50-94 fell from 22.93 to 21.78 while the profile gained GSMem::writeImageTransfer 5.2% and IopKernel::beginNextReady 3.4%, both absent from the MFIFO profile. advanceEeTimers went from 2.6% to below 0.5%. The batch was kept because late_irq was 0 and the fps dip matches the unowned GS/IOP change.

open: EeScheduler::accountCycles still calls advanceEeTimers on every dispatch and loop back-edge. That file is not owned. The batch is only inside advanceEeTimers.
GS mutex, VU1Interpreter::resetScheduler, and runNative were in the analysis and are not owned.
About 16% of UNPACK vectors on the baseline classifier were not 32-bit eligible (slow=5457293 of ~33.2e6). Those stay on the per-lane loop.
mfifoContigQwords returns one qword when rbor&rbsr != 0. The runs did not split how often that fallback hit.
PrintWindow never showed the menu or the fight, so a GS byte change would not show up in these shots.
The timer profile's new IopKernel and GSMem::writeImageTransfer symbols belong to the other tasks. They were not isolated.
GIF_STAT FQC is cleared only after processPendingTransfers sets m_gifFqcPending. The only writer in ps2_memory.cpp is that assignment. A writer in another file would leave FQC set.
